newsitem.title: UK: S&P affirms Flemish Community AA plus long-term.
newsitem.headline: S&P affirms Flemish Community AA plus long-term.

text.p: Standard & Poor's said on Thursday it affirmed its AA plus long-term issuer credit rating of the Flemish Community.
The outlook is stable, S&P said in a statement.

"The rating is based on the Flemish Community's strong and diversified economic base, the transparency of Belgian local government financing which ensures a high stablility and predictability of revenues, the improvement of the Flemish Community's budgetary performance and a manageable debt burden," S&P said.

"The Flemish government's cost-containment strategy, in combination with the strength of the diverse economic base are expected to support the financial performance and the gradual reduction in the debt burden," the agency said.
S&P said with 5.8 million inhabitants, Flanders accounts for 58 percent of the population of Belgium and is the dominant economic region with about 60 percent of GDP.
"Flanders economic base is diversified. The tertiary sector is predominant with 65 percent of employment but these sevices are very much related to industrial activities."

"With 26 percent of employment in 1994, the industrial sector remains important and accounts for 70 percent of the Belgian industrial employment. This structure results in some cyclicality even though Flanders's economy generally outperforms Belgium," S&P said.
S&P said the Flemish Community's budgetary performance improved substantially in recent years.
"The future budgetary performance will rely largely on moderate expenditures which are not easy to cut," it said.
S&P said it will look for continued improvement in the budgetary performance and for a reduction in debt, currently manageable at 73 percent of revenues.
